title: The three-month rainfall share gap fell by 0.36 points across 48 US states between 1951-1980 and 1996-2025
abstract: We tested the gap between the annual precipitation share from the three wettest months and the largest share from three adjacent phases of the annual cycle. We used NOAA nClimDiv monthly values for 48 contiguous US states. From 1951-1980 to 1996-2025, the equal-state gap fell from 3.855 to 3.495 percentage points. The change was -0.360 points, with a conditional 95% five-year block interval of -0.614 to -0.108. All planned gap checks had negative intervals. The two share changes on their own were uncertain. A month-order reference was added after the primary result. It kept each annual set of amounts but removed seasonal order. The reference gap also fell. The adjusted change was -0.195 points, with limits of -0.555 to +0.154. Thus the raw gap result does not establish a change in seasonal grouping beyond changes in monthly amounts. One product, state means, selected eras, a circular annual cycle and conditional uncertainty limit the result. This is a seasonal-share benchmark, not a test of floods, water storage, forecasts or a physical cause. Code, aggregate results, source hashes, bootstrap indices, checks and figures are included.

display.caption: A month-order adjustment leaves the seasonal grouping change uncertain. The adjustment test was added after the primary result. Limits are conditional 95% five-year block intervals.
